name: Congenital Myasthenic Syndrome with Kinetic Defect

diagnosticCriteria.formalCriteriaName: Diagnostic criteria for congenital myasthenic syndromes

criteria.description: Presence of fatigable muscle weakness with onset in infancy or early childhood
Electromyography showing decremental response on repetitive nerve stimulation
Identification of pathogenic variants in genes associated with kinetic defects of neuromuscular transmission
Improvement of symptoms with acetylcholinesterase inhibitors or other CMS-specific therapies

diagnosticCriteria.minimumForDiagnosis: Presence of fatigable muscle weakness with electrophysiological evidence plus pathogenic genetic variant confirmation
diagnosticCriteria.notes: Diagnosis requires integration of clinical, electrophysiological, and genetic data.

searchTerms: muscle weakness that worsens with use

pathognomonic.symptomName: Abnormal neuromuscular transmission kinetics demonstrated electrophysiologically
pathognomonic.notes: Characteristic kinetic defect on single-fiber EMG or repetitive nerve stimulation
searchTerms: abnormal timing of nerve to muscle signal transmission
electrophysiological evidence of impaired neuromuscular function

common.symptomName: Dysphagia due to bulbar muscle involvement
searchTerms: difficulty swallowing due to throat muscle weakness

common.symptomName: Respiratory muscle weakness causing exertional dyspnea
searchTerms: breathing muscle weakness causing shortness of breath with activity
weak respiratory muscles leading to breathlessness

occasional.symptomName: Limb muscle atrophy secondary to chronic weakness
searchTerms: muscle wasting in limbs due to chronic weakness

occasional.symptomName: Mild scoliosis due to axial muscle weakness
searchTerms: mild spine curvature from weak core muscles
scoliosis caused by axial muscle weakness
spinal deformity related to trunk muscle weakness
slurred speech from throat muscle weakness
speech difficulties due to bulbar muscle problems

rare.symptomName: Severe respiratory failure requiring ventilatory support
searchTerms: life-threatening breathing failure needing ventilator support

rare.symptomName: Cardiac arrhythmias secondary to autonomic involvement
searchTerms: heart rhythm issues due to autonomic dysfunction
cardiac arrhythmias related to nerve involvement
thinking problems not caused by low oxygen
cognitive difficulties unrelated to breathing issues

imaging: Muscle MRI may show mild fatty infiltration in chronic cases
Chest imaging to assess respiratory muscle status if indicated
genetic: Pathogenic variants in genes affecting neuromuscular junction kinetics (e.g., CHAT, RAPSN, DOK7 mutations)
other: Electrophysiological studies showing decremental response on repetitive nerve stimulation
Single-fiber electromyography demonstrating increased jitter and blocking

distinguishingFeatures: Multi-system involvement including CNS and cardiac
Muscle biopsy showing ragged red fibers

redFlags: Bulbar muscle paralysis with aspiration risk
Lack of response to acetylcholinesterase inhibitors
